uc1.title: Use case 1 — Temporal dynamics
uc1.alt: Use case 1 — Temporal dynamics: annual growth of light
uc1.caption: Between 2014 and 2025, night-time light in Namibia changed by +5.6% per year (95% CI: +4.1% to +6.4%). Over the last 12 months, the seasonally adjusted level is -1.6% relative to the previous 12 months. (confidence high: significant trend (p < 0.01; n = 12))
uc1.source: VIIRS DNB monthly (VCMSLCFG) · NOAA/EOG · Google Earth Engine

uc3.title: Use case 3 — Lights and GDP
uc3.alt: Use case 3 — Lights and GDP: light–GDP elasticity
uc3.caption: The elasticity of light with respect to real GDP is 1.85 in levels (95% CI: −0.48 to 4.17, R² = 0.22, 12 years) and −0.24 in growth rates (CI: −0.82 to 0.33). Out of sample, light growth tracks GDP growth with a correlation of −0.55 (mean absolute error: 3.6 percentage points of growth). (confidence low: n = 12, not significant (p = 0.12))

uc4.title: Use case 4 — Economic shocks
uc4.alt: Use case 4 — Economic shocks: shock trough
uc4.caption: The most pronounced shock in the seasonally adjusted series is “COVID-19”: trough of -2.9% (03/2021), return to the pre-shock level after 13 months. (confidence low: trough compared with pre-shock month-to-month variability)
uc4.source: VIIRS DNB monthly (VCMSLCFG) · NOAA/EOG · Google Earth Engine

uc6.title: Use case 6 — Industrial zones
uc6.alt: Use case 6 — Industrial zones: industrial clusters
uc6.caption: 45 industrial clusters detected from concordant satellite signals: 10 heavy industry, 10 business parks & logistics, 8 oil & gas sites and 17 isolated sites to verify. They emit 17.8% of national light (latest year); their light changes by +2.0% per year. Oshana has the most industrial activity. (confidence low: precision 51% and recall 14% against the reference list)
